title: NYC Comptroller Levine urges Anthropic to pause US IPO
source_used: PYMNTS (summarising the 14 Oct letter; Reuters and CNBC carried it)
key_facts: New York City Comptroller Mark Levine called on Anthropic to delay its initial public offering (IPO) and focus on AI safety issues the company itself has highlighted.
He wrote on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026 to Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei; the letter is posted on the Comptroller's website.
Levine cited a 12 Sep essay in which Amodei said the industry "must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models".
He also cited reports that Anthropic's draft S-1 filing has 80 pages of risk disclosures saying AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity".
He asked Anthropic to disclose how it will implement audits and controls, their scope and a projected timeline.
Levine is investment adviser, custodian and trustee of New York City pension funds with over $325 billion in assets.
Anthropic said in June it filed confidentially for an IPO; Bloomberg reported on 1 Oct it aims to begin trading before Thanksgiving. Anthropic did not immediately comment.
quote_evidence: Levine made this call in a Wednesday (Oct. 14) letter addressed to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and posted on the New York City Comptroller's website.
The demands of preparing for a public offering diverts resources and attention from this very necessary work.
why_it_matters_hint: A major public pension overseer is publicly pressing the AI lab on safety governance before it lists.
